Physicians are not entirely aware of the side effects of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. While there was a poor knowledge of some side effects, such as chronic cough and angioedema, this may be due to underrepresentation in local healthcare datasets.

However, specific details about ACE-1 gene polymorphism and its potential role in chronic kidney disease among hypertensive patients are more nuanced. A study concluded that the ACE-DD genotype may be a risk factor for causing or developing chronic kidney failure in hypertensive patients.

Regarding primary care physicians' efforts to meet the needs of family caregivers of the frail elderly, it is hypothesized that these individuals often face challenges due to lack of interest from their medical providers and potential underremuneration for counseling sessions. Additionally, being a professional caregiver can be demanding on its own.

Finally, about aromatase inhibitor-related musculoskeletal symptoms, patients who develop osteoporosis are at increased risk of experiencing these symptoms. Complementary therapies like calcium/bisphosphonates (Ca/Bis) have been found to reduce the incidence of such symptoms and fractures.
